penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: An E2EE SDK is a software engineering artifact — creating and maintaining actual cryptographic libraries, client SDKs for three platforms, and security documentation requires deep developer work per release cycle, not automatable by Claude prompts.

rationale: The buyer is clear (a dev team with a real compliance deadline and budget) and willingness to pay is credible since E2EE is a sales gate for enterprise contracts. However, the core deliverable is a production-grade cryptographic SDK across three platforms (Electron, React Native, NestJS) — this is a serious engineering artifact that cannot be shipped as Claude prompts + a landing page; it needs expert security engineering and ongoing maintenance. Buildability and operational autonomy score rock-bottom, making this fundamentally a wrong fit for a solo non-technical operator running an AI factory.
solution_plan: This opportunity is NOT viable for a solo non-technical operator. The service would be a licensable E2EE SDK for NestJS/Electron/React Native stacks. Building it requires writing and auditing production cryptographic code across three platforms — work that demands a senior security engineer and carries serious liability if done wrong. Claude cannot generate and maintain a trustworthy crypto SDK autonomously. Even if built, ongoing support (security patches, platform updates, customer integration help) requires deep human expertise per customer. Recommend dropping this opportunity entirely.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (score 2, min 6) and operational_autonomy (score 2, min 7). Both are hard build_gates. Also applies requires_human_fulfillment penalty. The idea itself is a real market gap but is the wrong shape for this factory.
